readerMoment: Curious about home network security and willing to buy a small router or a Raspberry Pi. Has used a terminal, but has never watched their own network traffic.
outcome: Can set up an isolated lab segment, inventory the listening services on a machine they own, and choose a first sensor or decoy safely.

prerequisites.idea: Consent and scope: which devices and traffic you may observe
IP addresses, subnets, and what a router does between networks
Ports, processes, and what it means for a service to listen
Firewall rules, and how to test one from both sides
VLANs, guest networks, and why a Wi-Fi repeater may not isolate
Running commands with admin rights on Linux, macOS, or Windows

teachingShape.realTask: Build a small defensive lab at home without touching anyone else's traffic
demonstrate: Listener inventory commands for three operating systems
integrate: Draw your own network and inventory one machine

requiredIdeas: Separate the lab behind a boundary you control
Give each part one job: router, mirror port, sensor, decoy
Inventory listening services and keep a dated baseline
Choose between Zeek, Suricata, OpenCanary, and Cowrie
Contain the honeypot: isolated, outbound denied, no real secrets
Grow the lab by evidence, one stage at a time
visualNeeds: The topology: upstream network, lab router, trusted devices, sensor, and isolated decoy, with the blocked path shown

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Testing devices or traffic you do not own
deliberatelyExcluded.why: Out of scope by consent, not by size.

deliberatelyExcluded.what: Exposing a honeypot to the internet
deliberatelyExcluded.why: Deferred until the reader knows the logs and failure modes.
